mainTopic: The penalty for a נזיר coming from outside ארץ ישראל, רבי יהודה's view on הילני המלכה, and witnesses who disagree about how many terms of נזירות were vowed.
overview: The גמרא first finishes a suggestion that בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about whether the decree on land outside ארץ ישראל covers its earth or its air. It rejects that suggestion: everyone agrees the decree is about the earth, and they argue only about how big the penalty is. Next it asks whether רבי יהודה's count of fourteen years for הילני המלכה assumes she became impure, following בית שמאי, or that she did not, following בית הלל. The exact number fourteen in the משנה, and a ברייתא from רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אליעזר, both show that he follows בית הלל. A new משנה then brings two sets of witnesses, one saying a man vowed two terms of נזירות and the other saying five. בית שמאי say the testimony is split, and בית הלל say two is included in five. A ברייתא moves this argument to a single set where the two witnesses disagree. Finally רב teaches that everyone agrees the testimony is split in a case of 'counting', where each witness heard different numbers counted out.

steps.title: Suggestion: בית הלל think the decree was about the air
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a suggested explanation. Maybe בית הלל hold the decree on land outside ארץ ישראל covers even its air, which makes it a stronger impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do בית הלל hold that the Sages made their decree because of the air of that land?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a proposed reason for the argument in the משנה. The proposal is that בית הלל think the decree covers the airspace of land outside ארץ ישראל. The next step will test this proposal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the decree covers even the air, the impurity is more serious. That would explain why בית הלל make the נזיר start his whole term again. By contrast, בית שמאי would hold the decree is only about the earth, so they require just thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: Airspace, the air above a land
The Sages decreed, made a rabbinic rule
They hold, they are of the opinion

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel hold:
they decreed on it because of its airspace?
phrases.notes: "It" means land outside ארץ ישראל, which the Sages declared impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי: מִשּׁוּם אַוֵּירָא גָּזְרוּ עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the suggestion begun just before this passage, which tied the argument to earth versus air.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל really about whether the decree covers the earth or the air?

steps.title: Everyone agrees it is about the earth; they argue about the penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earth-versus-air explanation. Both sides agree the decree is about the earth. They only argue about how much to penalize: thirty days, or the whole term again.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees the decree was about the earth. בית שמאי hold we penalize him with a regular, unspecified נזירות of thirty days. בית הלל hold that when we penalize, he goes back to the start of his נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. It says there is no argument about earth versus air. The argument is only about the size of the קנס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed disagreement about how strong the impurity is gets removed. Instead, both sides accept the same kind of impurity, and the disagreement moves to the penalty. בית שמאי give the shortest standard term, thirty days. בית הלל make him redo his entire original term.

keyTerms.meaning: Unspecified נזירות, which lasts thirty days

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree the decree is about the earth. They argue only about the penalty: בית שמאי say thirty days, and בית הלל say the full term again.

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees
that they decreed on it because of its earth,
and Beit Shammai hold
that we penalize with an unspecified naziriteship,
phrases.notes: A נזירות with no length stated lasts thirty days.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel hold:
when we penalize, it is back to the beginning of the naziriteship.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִשּׁוּם גּוּשָׁהּ גָּזְרוּ עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the earth-versus-air explanation proposed in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the argument depends on whether the decree covers the air.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained entirely by a different view of how big the penalty should be, with both sides agreeing the decree is about the earth.

steps.title: Which case was רבי יהודה describing for הילני המלכה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the story of הילני המלכה. It asks whether רבי יהודה's fourteen years assumes she became impure and follows בית שמאי, or that she did not become impure and follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: There was an incident with Queen הילני, and so on. They asked: Was רבי יהודה talking about a case where she became impure, following בית שמאי? Or a case where she did not become impure, following בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the opening of the הילני המלכה story from the משנה. Then it asks how to understand רבי יהודה's view that she was a נזירה for only fourteen years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to reach fourteen years. Option one: by בית שמאי she owed only thirty days in ארץ ישראל, then became impure and had to redo her seven years. Option two: by בית הלל she did seven more years in the land and never became impure, so seven plus seven equals fourteen.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened
A question was raised before them

phrases.english: An incident with Queen Helene, etc.
A question was raised before them:
Is it where she became impure, and according to Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: The question is about רבי יהודה's count of fourteen years, from the end of the משנה.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is where she did not become impure,
and according to Beit Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בְּשֶׁנִּטְמֵאת, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the penalty rules just explained to ask what רבי יהודה's fourteen years assumes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה's fourteen years assume impurity and בית שמאי, or no impurity and בית הלל?

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: the number fourteen fits only בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings proof from the משנה. Under the בית שמאי reading, the total would be fourteen years and thirty days, not just fourteen years. So רבי יהודה must follow בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: She went up to the land, and בית הלל ruled she should be a נזירה another seven years, and so on. If you think רבי יהודה meant she became impure, following בית שמאי, then why does he say she was a נזירה only fourteen years? He should have said fourteen years and thirty days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ראיה from the exact number רבי יהודה gives. That number does not work under the בית שמאי option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By בית שמאי, she would first have kept thirty days in ארץ ישראל. Only then would she have become impure and redone her seven years. That gives seven years, plus thirty days, plus seven years. Since רבי יהודה says exactly fourteen, he must mean seven plus seven by בית הלל, with no impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: They ruled for her, instructed her

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's fourteen years means seven years abroad plus seven years in ארץ ישראל by בית הלל, and she did not become impure.

phrases.english: Come and hear: She went up to the Land,
and Beit Hillel instructed her
that she should be a nazirite again
for another seven years, etc.
And if you would think it is where she became impure
and according to Beit Shammai, if so,
"Rabbi Yehuda says

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיְתָה נְזִירָה אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה״?
phrases.english: she was a nazirite for only fourteen years"?

phrases.aramaic: ״אַרְבַּע עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: He should have said "fourteen years and thirty days"!
phrases.notes: The extra thirty days are the ones בית שמאי require on arriving in the land, before she became impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by checking the arithmetic of רבי יהודה's number.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה follows בית הלל and holds she did not become impure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording that רבי יהודה said exactly fourteen years, without adding thirty days.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs this up: impurity at the end means only a thirty-day נזירות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the conclusion. רבי יהודה, in the name of רבי אליעזר, learns from the פסוק that someone who becomes impure on the day his term ends keeps only a regular thirty-day נזירות. So the בית שמאי reading would not lead to fourteen years.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי אליעזר, the פסוק says "This is the law of the נזיר." התורה means: if he became impure on the day his term was completed, give him the law of a regular נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as extra support that רבי יהודה cannot be following the בית שמאי reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יהודה's own rule, impurity on the last day of a term requires only a regular thirty-day נזירות, not the whole term again. So if she became impure at the end of the thirty days בית שמאי require, she would add only thirty days, not seven years. Fourteen years must therefore come from בית הלל's seven extra years, with no impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: This is also taught in a ברייתא
The day of completion, the last day of the term
The law of a נזיר, here a regular thirty-day נזירות

steps.whatToRemember: By רבי יהודה's view, impurity on the final day only requires a regular thirty-day נזירות. This confirms he follows בית הלל in the story of הילני המלכה.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:
For the verse says: "This is the law of the nazirite,"
the Torah is saying:
when he becomes impure on the day of completion,
give him the law of a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that supports the conclusion of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's fourteen years cannot be explained by the בית שמאי reading with impurity.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אליעזר, reading the פסוק "זאת תורת הנזיר" (במדבר 6:13).

steps.title: New משנה: two sets of witnesses say two terms or five terms
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents two sets of witnesses. One set says the man vowed two terms of נזירות and the other says five. בית שמאי say there is no נזירות at all, and בית הלל say he keeps two.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two sets of witnesses testify about a man, one saying he vowed two terms of נזירות and the other saying five, בית שמאי say the testimony is split and there is no נזירות. בית הלל say two is included in five, so he is a נזיר for two terms.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a dispute about witnesses who disagree on the number of terms of נזירות someone vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי see the two testimonies as clashing, so neither one stands. בית הלל see a shared part: both sets agree he vowed at least two terms. So the two terms that everyone agrees on are binding.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets (groups) of witnesses, each made up of two witnesses
The testimony is split, meaning the testimonies contradict each other

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי עֵדִים
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who had two sets of witnesses
testifying about him,
these testify that he vowed two terms of נזירות,
and these testify that he vowed five,
Beit Shammai say: The testimony is split,
and there is no naziriteship here at all.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: יֵשׁ בִּכְלַל חָמֵשׁ שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: Two is included in five,
so that he is a nazirite for two terms.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי עֵדִים מְעִידוֹת אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the הילני המלכה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: contradicting sets cancel each other and there is no נזירות. בית הלל: the shared two terms are binding.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the argument is really about one set of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה does not follow רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. He holds that with two sets of witnesses, everyone agrees two is included in five. The argument is only about two witnesses in a single set who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like this תנא. רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about two sets of witnesses, one saying two and one saying five. There, everyone agrees two is included in five. They argued about one set, where one witness says two and the other says five. בית שמאי say their testimony is split, and בית הלל say two is included in five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a ברייתא tells the story of this argument differently from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two full sets, each set is a complete testimony, so even בית שמאי accept the overlapping two terms. In one set, each single witness is only half of a testimony. If the two witnesses do not match, בית שמאי say there is no valid testimony at all. So the ברייתא moves the dispute to the case of a single set.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow this תנא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the משנה the dispute is about two sets, and in the ברייתא it is about two witnesses in one set. In the ברייתא, everyone agrees about two sets.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא,
phrases.english: GEMARA: Our mishna is not in accordance with this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about two sets of witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת שְׁתַּיִם, וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת חָמֵשׁ,
phrases.english: one set saying two and one set saying five,
that two is included in five.
About what did they disagree?
About one set of witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר שְׁתַּיִם, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר חָמֵשׁ,
phrases.english: where one witness says two and one witness says five,
that Beit Shammai say: Their testimony is split.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: יֵשׁ בִּכְלַל חָמֵשׁ שְׁתַּיִם.
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: Two is included in five.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that changes which case the dispute in the משנה is about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With two sets, everyone agrees he keeps two terms. With one set whose witnesses disagree, בית שמאי say there is no testimony and בית הלל say he keeps two.

steps.title: רב: everyone agrees in a case of counting
steps.stepSummary: רב adds that in a case of 'counting', everyone agrees, including בית הלל. Following the ברייתא's case of one set, the testimony there is split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Everyone agrees in a case of counting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב makes a short statement that limits בית הלל's rule. It sets up the next question about what he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל usually say the two terms everyone agrees on are binding. רב says there is a type of case, 'counting', where even בית הלל agree the testimony falls apart. The next steps explain what 'counting' means, and step 11 gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting. The case where the person counted out his terms one by one

phrases.english: Rav said:
All agree in a case of counting.
phrases.notes: "All" means even בית הלל agree the testimonies contradict each other here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to בית הלל's rule about the case in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a case of counting, even בית הלל agree the testimony is split.

steps.title: רב חמא asks what רב meant
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא asks רב חסדא what case רב is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא said to רב חסדא: What is רב saying?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא asks what 'counting' means in רב's statement. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's word 'counting' is unclear. So the גמרא will test one possible reading, reject it, and then give the right one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama said to Rav Ḥisda:
What is he saying?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of 'counting' is רב describing?

steps.title: It cannot mean witnesses who openly deny each other
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion is that one witness says 'five and not two' and the other says 'two and not five'. This is rejected, because those witnesses clearly contradict each other. רב would not need to say that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say one witness says five and not two, and the other says two and not five, then they clearly contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one reading of רב and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each witness openly rules out the other's number, there is no shared part left. Of course even בית הלל would throw out that testimony. So רב must be teaching something less obvious.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר חָמֵשׁ וְלֹא שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: If we say: One says five and not two,
and one says two and not five,
they are contradicting one another!
phrases.notes: The point is that this is too obvious. רב would not need to teach it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר חָמֵשׁ וְלֹא שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a first answer to רב חמא's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading רב as talking about witnesses who explicitly deny each other's number.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is an obvious contradiction, so רב's statement would teach nothing new.

steps.title: Counting means each witness heard different numbers counted out
steps.stepSummary: רב means a case where the man counted out his terms. One witness heard him count 'one, two' and the other heard 'three, four, five'. They are describing different counting, so even בית הלל agree the testimony is split.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, one witness says he counted one and two, and the other says he counted three, four, five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of רב's 'counting' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the normal case, 'two' fits inside 'five', so בית הלל find a shared part. Here, each witness heard different numbers counted out: one heard only one and two, and the other heard only three, four, five. Nothing overlaps, so there is no shared part to rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings in the correct explanation

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's rule that two is included in five works only when one number fits inside the other. When each witness describes different numbers being counted out, even בית הלל agree the testimony is split.

phrases.english: Rather: One says one and two,
phrases.notes: He means this witness heard the man count out only terms one and two.

phrases.english: and one says three, four, five.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Counting is a case where the witnesses heard different numbers counted out, so their testimonies do not overlap.
